accepted.question_text: For symmetric deterministic tensors T1, ..., Tn in (R^d)^(otimes r) and iid standard Gaussian random variables g1, ..., gn, define the symmetric injective l_p norm by ||T||_{I_p} = max_{||x||_p <= 1} |<T, x^(otimes r)>| for p >= 2. Is it true that E ||sum_i g_i T_i||_{I_p} is at most O~_{r,p}(d^(1/2-1/p) (sum_i ||T_i||_{I_p}^2)^(1/2)), where O~_{r,p} hides constants depending on r and p and polylogarithmic factors in d and n?

evidence.quote: Here ||x||p = (Pdi=1 |xi|p)1/p denotes the l_p norm and ||Ti||Ip = max||x||p<=1 |<Ti, x^(otimes r)>| is the symmetric injective l_p norm.
Conjecture 16 (Type-2 constant of Tensors). Let p >= 2, then E ||sum_i gi Ti||Ip <= O~_{r,p}( d^(1/2 - 1/p) sqrt(sum_i ||Ti||Ip^2) ).

accepted.question_text: Let vartheta(G) be the Lovasz theta number defined by vartheta(G) = max {sum_{i,j} X_ij : X is positive semidefinite, Tr X = 1, and X_ij = 0 for every edge (i,j) of G}. If G is an Erdos-Renyi random graph G(n, 1/2), is E vartheta(G) = (1 + o(1)) sqrt(n)?

evidence.quote: Lovasz number is a natural semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation: vartheta(G) := max_X { sum_{i,j} Xij , such that X >= 0, Tr X = 1, and Xij = 0 for all (i, j) in E(G) }.
Conjecture 17. Let G be distributed as G(n, 1/2). Then, E vartheta(G) = (1 + o(1)) sqrt(n).

accepted.question_text: A circulant graph on n vertices is a graph on Z_n whose adjacency relation is invariant under cyclic shifts. A random dense circulant graph is generated by choosing a vector x in {0,1}^{ceil((n-1)/2)} uniformly at random, where x_k = 1 means that vertex 0 is adjacent to k and the symmetry (0,k) in E(G) iff (0,n-k) in E(G) is enforced. For such a random graph G, is E vartheta(G) = (1 + o(1)) sqrt(n)?
accepted.context_brief: Lovasz number of random circulant graphs

evidence.quote: To sample a random circulant graph, we only need to sample the neighbors of a single vertex, say vertex 0. Since (0, k) in E(G) implies that (0, n - k) in E(G), we sample a vector x in {0, 1}^{ceil((n-1)/2)} uniformly at random, and xk = 1 stands for (0, k) in E(G).
Conjecture 18. Let G be distributed as a random dense circulant graph. Then, E vartheta(G) = (1 + o(1)) sqrt(n).

accepted.question_text: Let N = 4M - 5 and draw A in C^(N x M) at random so that im(A) is uniformly distributed among M-dimensional subspaces of C^(4M-5). If p_M is the probability that the phaseless map x mod T -> |Ax|^2 is injective, is it true that p_M < 1 for every M and that p_M tends to 0 as M tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: Given A in K^(N x M), the Phase Retrieval Problem aims to recover a vector x in K^M from |Ax|. One can only hope to recover x modulo T_K.
Conjecture 19. Let N = 4M - 5 and draw A in C^(N x M) at random ... Let pM be the probability that the mapping x mod T -> |Ax|^2 is injective. (a) pM < 1 for all M. (b) lim_{M->infty} pM = 0.

accepted.question_text: Let MUB(d) denote the largest number of orthonormal bases in C^d that are pairwise mutually unbiased, meaning that whenever vectors are taken from two different bases their inner products all have magnitude 1/sqrt(d). Is MUB(6) < 7?

evidence.quote: Two orthonormal bases {v1, . . . , vd}, {w1, . . . , wd} subset C^d are called mutually unbiased if |<vi, wj>| = 1/sqrt(d) for all i, j. Let MUB(d) denote the largest possible number of mutually unbiased bases in C^d.
Conjecture 22. Let MUB(d) denote the largest possible number of mutually unbiased bases in C^d. We have MUB(6) < 7.

accepted.question_text: Is there a degree-4 Sum-of-Squares proof that no 7 orthonormal bases in C^6 are pairwise mutually unbiased, i.e. that there is no collection of 7 bases in C^6 for which every cross-basis inner product has magnitude 1/sqrt(6)?

evidence.quote: Two orthonormal bases ... are called mutually unbiased if |<vi, wj>| = 1/sqrt(d) for all i, j.
Open Problem 23. Is there a Sum-of-Squares degree 4 proof that there are no 7 Mutually Unbiased Bases in C^6?

accepted.question_text: Does every dimension d admit an equiangular tight frame in C^d with exactly d^2 vectors, meaning a collection phi_1, ..., phi_{d^2} of unit vectors spanning C^d such that sum_i phi_i phi_i^* is a scalar multiple of the identity and |<phi_i, phi_j>| is the same for every i != j?

evidence.quote: A frame phi1, . . . , phin in C^d is an ETF if: it is unit-normed, it is a tight frame, and it is equiangular.
Conjecture 24 (Zauner's Conjecture). For each dimension d, there exists an ETF in C^d with n = d^2 vectors.

accepted.question_text: For a prime p congruent to 1 modulo 4, let G_p be the Paley graph on vertex set [p], where i and j are adjacent exactly when i - j is a quadratic residue modulo p. Is its clique number omega(G_p) bounded by a polylogarithm in p?

evidence.quote: Given a prime number p such that p == 1 (mod 4) the Paley graph on p nodes Gp is the graph where nodes i and j are connected if i - j is a quadratic residue modulo p.
Conjecture 25. Let omega(Gp) denote the clique number of the Paley Graph for p == 1 (mod 4) prime. omega(Gp) = O(polylog(p)).

accepted.question_text: Let G_{p,1} be the induced subgraph of the Paley graph G_p on the vertices adjacent to 0. As p tends to infinity through primes congruent to 1 modulo 4, is the Lovasz theta number of the complement of G_{p,1} asymptotic to sqrt(p/2)?

evidence.quote: Let Gp,1 denote the induced subgraph on the vertices adjacent to the node 0, which we call the 1-localization.
Conjecture 26. vartheta(Gp,1) ~ sqrt(p/2) (for p == 1 (mod 4) prime) where Gp,1 is the 1-localization of the Paley Graph described above.

accepted.question_text: Let G_{p,2} be the induced subgraph of the Paley graph G_p on the vertices adjacent to both 0 and 1. For all sufficiently large primes p congruent to 1 modulo 4, is the Lovasz theta number of the complement of G_{p,2} at most (2/3) sqrt(p)?

evidence.quote: Let Gp,2 denote the induced subgraph on the vertices adjacent to 0 and 1.
Conjecture 27. For p == 1 (mod 4) prime and large enough we have vartheta(Gp,2) <= 2/3 sqrt(p) where Gp,2 is the 2-localization of the Paley Graph described above.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist epsilon > 0 such that the degree-4 Sum-of-Squares relaxation for the clique number of the Paley graph always yields an upper bound O(p^(1/2-epsilon)) for primes p congruent to 1 modulo 4?

evidence.quote: A fascinating question is whether the degree-4 Sum-of-Squares relaxation significantly improves on the sqrt(p) bound.
Conjecture 28. There exists epsilon > 0 such that the Sum-of-Squares relaxation of degree 4 for the clique number of the Paley graph gives a bound of O(p^(1/2-epsilon)).

accepted.question_text: For a prime p congruent to 1 modulo 4, consider the Paley equiangular tight frame obtained from quadratic-residue rows of the discrete Fourier transform and having (p+1) vectors in C^((p+1)/2). Does this construction satisfy the Restricted Isometry Property beyond the square-root bottleneck, meaning that there exists epsilon > 0 such that for m ~ p^(1/2+epsilon), every submatrix formed by choosing m distinct frame vectors has condition number bounded by a constant independent of p?
accepted.context_brief: Restricted isometry of the Paley ETF

evidence.quote: For p == 1 (mod 4) prime the Paley ETF ... is an Equiangular Tight Frame with n = p + 1 vectors in C^((p+1)/2).
Conjecture 29. The Paley Equiangular Tight Frame construction satisfies the Restricted Isometry Property beyond the square-root bottleneck.

accepted.question_text: For a log-concave probability measure mu on R^n, let psi_mu = inf_{S subseteq R^n} mu^+(S) / min{mu(S), mu(R^n \ S)} be its isoperimetric constant, and let A be its covariance matrix. Is there a universal constant C > 0 such that psi_mu is always bounded below by C / sqrt(||A||_op), equivalently up to universal constants by the best half-space isoperimetric ratio?

evidence.quote: The isoperimetric constant psi_mu is the minimal boundary measure among sets S with mu(S) >= 1/2: psi_mu := inf_S mu^+(S) / min{mu(S), mu(R^n\S)}.

Conjecture 30 (KLS Conjecture). There exists a universal constant C > 0 such that for every log-concave measure mu ... Equivalently, there exists a universal constant C > 0 such that psi_mu >= C / sqrt(||A||_op).

accepted.question_text: Fix a finite shape alpha with left vertex set U_alpha and right vertex set V_alpha. Let M_alpha be the random graph matrix obtained by summing over all injective realizations phi : V(alpha) -> [n] the rank-one terms (product over edges (i,j) of epsilon_{phi(i),phi(j)}) e_{phi(U_alpha)} e_{phi(V_alpha)}^T, where the epsilon_{i,j} are independent Rademacher signs. Are there functions f and g depending only on alpha such that E ||M_alpha|| = Theta(n^{f(alpha)} (log n)^{g(alpha)})?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp norm bounds for graph matrices

evidence.quote: Definition 14.2 (Graph matrices). ... The graph matrix M_alpha is the n^{|U_alpha|} x n^{|V_alpha|} random matrix ... given by M_alpha = sum_realization phi (prod_{(i,j) in E(alpha)} epsilon_{phi(i),phi(j)}) e_{phi(U_alpha)} e_{phi(V_alpha)}^top.
Conjecture 31 (Sharp graph matrix bounds). There are functions f and g depending only on the shape alpha, such that E ||M_alpha|| = Theta( n^{f(alpha)} (log n)^{g(alpha)} ).

needs_review.question_text_raw: There exist universal constants C > 0 and 0 < beta < 1 such that, for any M > 1 and A in R^((2M-1) x M) ... omega(A) <= C max_{k in [N]} ||A_k|| beta^M.

evidence.quote: Definition 10.1. Given A in R^(N x M) let omega(A) be defined as omega(A) = min_{S subseteq [N]: rank(A_{S^c})<n} sigma_M(A_S), where A_S denotes the submatrix made of the rows indexed by S.
Conjecture 20. There exist universal constants C > 0 and 0 < beta < 1 such that, for any M > 1 and A in R^((2M-1) x M) ... omega(A) <= C max_{k in [N]} ||A_k|| beta^M.

needs_review.question_text_raw: What is the value of omega(A) for A with iid standard gaussian entries? Does it satisfy the bound in the conjecture? If so, what is beta?

evidence.quote: Definition 10.1. Given A in R^(N x M) let omega(A) be defined as omega(A) = min_{S subseteq [N]: rank(A_{S^c})<n} sigma_M(A_S).
Open Problem 21. What is the value of omega(A) for A with iid standard gaussian entries? Does it satisfy the bound in the conjecture? If so, what is beta?
